results.fact: Identity and location of the crux
results.evidence: The Mountaineers standard-south-route trip report (surfaced in search snippets; the page itself returns 403) describes going straight up-center from the upper meadow to 'the hourglass', a short pitch of class 4, while a first-timer blog calls the Catwalk 'probably the most challenging, or at least a tie' and pictures the Dog Walk Ledge separately on the descent. Other reports reachable this pass (onehikeaweek, WTA, stevensong index) name no crux. So the two named features are both described as the hardest spot by different parties and no two sources agree on one crux. To settle it: a full route description (e.g. the Mountaineers route page or SummitPost, both 403 here) that places the Hourglass relative to the Catwalk and says which is the crux.

results.correct_value: Best July-September (season Jun-Sep); October good but can see early snow
results.evidence: Inside the row, climate.bySeason.summer says July-September is the prime dry window, monthBreakdown marks July, August and September optimal with October only 'good', best_season runs the prime window through September, and itinerary.cal says summer/early fall. The outliers are the header's 'best Jul-Aug' (copied into the primary approach variant) and optimalWindow's 'July through October' (copied into seasonal_hazards.weather.typical). One outside peak-weather page gives best months to climb as July, August, September. WTA confirms summer scree vs. snow-otherwise but gives no months.

results.fact: Descent loss vs gain on an out-and-back
results.evidence: WTA gives 3,190 ft gain over 4.0 mi RT and onehikeaweek 3,150 ft gain; no outside source states a car-to-car descent (loss) figure for this route, so under the standing rule loss_ft is not set from gain. To settle it: a GPS track or report stating total descent for this route.

The Mountain Project route page speaks of 'as few as two placements in a 60m pitch' and three 30 m rappels, while the Simmons Mountain Works report used only 40 m of a 70 m rope for the whole route and recommends a 40 m lead line plus a 30 m rap line. The CascadeClimbers 2015 TR (which would be a third party) did not load. The sources still disagree on whether pitches exceed 40 m. To settle it: a second independent report stating pitch lengths or the rope actually needed.

results.correct_value: Group size capped at 12 people / 8 stock in the Mount Skokomish Wilderness.
results.evidence: Already resolved: access.rules now reads 'Group size capped at 12 people / 8 stock in the Mount Skokomish Wilderness.' with no national-park rules. The Forest Service's Mount Skokomish Wilderness page and its Olympic NF wilderness page both prohibit groups of more than 12 persons and/or 8 head of livestock, so the current text agrees.

One GPS-tracked report gives 6 miles / 4,250 ft trailhead-to-Ellinor-summit; another gives about 2 miles between the summits; a Strava-style record on The Wild Outsiders logs 12.32 mi / 5,571 ft for its whole outing; a guide-service blog gives only 2 miles for the Washington trail. No two sources agree on either the one-way figure or the waypoint mileages. To settle it: a second GPS track clearly measured trailhead to Ellinor summit and on to the Ellinor upper trailhead.

The only split-time report gives 4.25 hr total with '1.5 hrs to Washington, 3.25 hrs to Ellinor' (ambiguous whether 3.25 is cumulative); Mountain Project summaries give 3.5-4.5 hr for the traverse; The Wild Outsiders logged 8.4 hr moving time; a guide blog calls it a half-day. No two sources agree on a total. To settle it: a second report with trailhead-to-Ellinor-summit and car-to-car times.

results.correct_value: Group size capped at 12 people / 8 stock in the Mount Skokomish Wilderness; no open fires above 3,500 ft (stoves only).
results.evidence: access.rules quotes Olympic National Park rules (designated group sites for 7+, park-wide bear canisters) although the row's own land manager and permit zone are Olympic National Forest, Mount Skokomish Wilderness. The Forest Service's Mount Skokomish Wilderness page prohibits groups over 12 persons and/or 8 head of livestock and fires above 3,500 ft (stoves only); the Olympic NF wilderness page states the same group and fire limits and that no permit is needed. The SE Ridge row on the same peak already carries the corrected group-size rule.
